parsed.rationale: Customer reports being charged twice for an annual plan renewal on May 1 and requests reversing one charge and confirming which invoice (INV-9031 or INV-9032) should remain.

parsed.draft_response:
Hi there—thanks for flagging this. I’m sorry for the confusion caused by the duplicate annual plan charges on May 1.

I see you’ve provided invoice numbers INV-9031 and INV-9032. To make sure we reverse the correct transaction and confirm the one you should keep in your accounting, could you please confirm:
1) Which invoice should be reversed (INV-9031 or INV-9032)?
2) The amount shown on each invoice (INV-9031 amount and INV-9032 amount).
3) The last 4 digits of the card that was charged (so we can match the payments).
4) Whether both charges show as completed successfully on your side, or if one is pending/failed.

Once we have the above, we’ll route this for billing review to reconcile the two invoices and advise which one should remain.
promised_actions: Escalate/review the duplicate charges with the billing team to reconcile INV-9031 vs INV-9032
Advise which invoice should remain in the customer’s accounting after verification
safety_notes: No promise of a refund or reversal is made until the customer confirms which invoice should be reversed and we can match the charges.
No assumption is made about the payment status (completed vs pending/failed) or the exact amounts; these are requested for reconciliation.
Acknowledges that billing review/escalation is required without claiming resolution.

parsed.customer_impact: Potential incorrect billing/duplicate payment for the annual plan renewal, requiring reversal of one charge and clarity on which invoice should be retained for accounting.
grounded_facts: The customer reports being charged twice for an annual plan renewal.
The double charge occurred on May 1.
The invoice numbers provided are INV-9031 and INV-9032.
The customer is requesting that one of the charges be reversed.
The customer is requesting confirmation of which invoice should remain in their accounting system.
missing_information: Which specific charge should be reversed (INV-9031 or INV-9032) per the customer’s preference.
Whether both charges were processed successfully or if one is pending/failed.
The amounts charged on INV-9031 and INV-9032.
The card/account identifier on which the charges occurred (e.g., last 4 digits) to match the transactions.
Any dates/timestamps of the two billing events beyond May 1 (e.g., exact times) to help reconcile records.
Whether the customer has already disputed either charge with their bank/card issuer.
risk_signals: Billing ambiguity due to two invoices for the same renewal date (INV-9031 vs INV-9032).
Renewal pressure/financial impact from potential duplicate charges.
Operational risk of reversing the wrong invoice if the correct one is not confirmed.
parsed.summary: The customer reports their card was charged twice for the annual plan renewal on May 1 and requests reversing one charge and confirming whether invoice INV-9031 or INV-9032 should remain.
